title: Nuclear extraction using opti-prep gradient centrifugation for 10X Genomics Multiome Assay
author: Lite Yang
materials: Prepare buffers and store them On ice .
Gather samples and store on dry ice.
Quick spin and aspire out PBS.
Carefully remove the supernatant without disturbing the pellet.

steps.title: Prepare Opti-Prep Gradient
steps.instruction: Layer iodixanol solutions in an ultracentrifuge tube to create a density gradient.

substeps.instruction: Layer 1 mL of 40% iodixanol at the bottom of the tube.
Slowly add 1 mL of 30% iodixanol on top, pipetting against the wall to maintain two distinct layers.
Keep the tube on ice (pre-indent ice with another tube to avoid disruption).

steps.title: Prepare Reagents and Equipment
steps.instruction: Prepare DTT and the ultracentrifuge for the run.

substeps.instruction: Thaw and dissolve DTT by incubating the tube at room temperature.
Place SW28 rotor into the ultracentrifuge and start a test run at 8900 rpm, 4 °C, for 1 hour.
Place douncers on ice.

steps.title: Tissue Preparation and Washing
steps.instruction: Thaw tissue and wash to remove OCT.

substeps.instruction: Take one sample from dry ice and thaw on ice for 1 minute.
Add 1 mL of 1X PBS to the original tube, pipet mix 10 times, and vortex for 5 seconds to wash off OCT.
Break down tissues by chopping the sample 30 times with clean scissors until trimmed into small pieces.
Repeat the PBS wash and chopping steps one more time.

steps.title: Tissue Homogenization
steps.instruction: Homogenize the tissue to release nuclei.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 mL of homogenization buffer and 10 µL of 10% NP40 to the sample.
Transfer the tissue to a 5 mL centrifuge tube using forceps.
Transfer samples to a pre-chilled douncer.
Insert loose pestle (“A”) and perform 15 strokes.
Perform 15 strokes with the tight pestle (“B”), minimizing bubble formation.

Optional: If big chunks are visible, let the douncer sit on ice for 1 minute, then perform an additional 5 strokes with tight pestle (“B”), rotating the pestle back and forth at the end of each stroke.

steps.title: Filtration and Resuspension
steps.instruction: Filter the homogenate and adjust the iodixanol concentration.

substeps.instruction: Filter the homogenate directly through a 50 µm Sysmex filter into a 2 mL centrifuge tube (use thumb pressure if debris is abundant).
Cap the tube and keep on ice.
Bring the sample volume up to 1 mL using resuspension buffer.
Vortex 50% iodixanol, then add 1 mL of freshly-vortexed 50% iodixanol to the homogenate to achieve a 25% iodixanol concentration.
Invert sample tubes 10 times to mix.

steps.title: Ultracentrifugation
steps.instruction: Perform density gradient centrifugation to isolate nuclei.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate 1.5 mL of the 25% iodixanol layer from the gradient tube (once the test spin is finished) to improve access to the interlayer.
Using a 1 mL pipette, slowly pipette 2 mL of nuclear resuspensions on top of the 30% layer, pipetting against the wall to maintain distinct layers.
Spin at 10,000 x g (8,900 rpm with SW28 rotor) for 18 minutes at 4 °C.
Insert the tube into the adaptor and seal the top with parafilm.
Adjust volume of samples with nuclease-free water to match the same level.

steps.title: Nuclei Recovery
steps.instruction: Collect the nuclei from the iodixanol interface.

substeps.instruction: Gently remove tubes from the centrifuge and remove supernatant by inverting, leaving 50 µL behind to avoid disturbing the pellet.
Centrifuge tubes at 500 x g, 4 °C, for 10 minutes (use a swinging bucket rotor for better efficiency).
Using a P200 pipette, stab the interface of 30% and 40% iodixanol; move the tip over the entire surface and aspirate 200 µL of the interlayer into a 2 mL centrifuge tube.
Repeat the interlayer collection 3 times to collect a total of 600 µL.
Dilute the collected iodixanol with 600 µL of Resuspension Buffer and 6 µL of 7-AAD ready-made solution (1 mg/ml stock, 5 ng/µL final concentration), then pipet mix 10 times.

steps.title: Nuclei Permeabilization and Washing
steps.instruction: Permeabilize nuclei and perform buffer exchange.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend pellets in 150 µL of resuspension buffer and pipet mix 10 times.
Add 20 µL of Nuclei Permeabilization Buffer (to a final concentration of 0.1 X) and mix by inverting 5 times.
Centrifuge at 500 x g, 4 °C, for 2 minutes to spin down excessive supernatant.
Remove most of the supernatant without disrupting the pellet.
Centrifuge tubes again at 500 x g, 4 °C, for 10 minutes.
Add 400 µL Diluted Nuclei Buffer to dilute the permeabilization buffer and facilitate exchange; mix by inverting 5 times.
Incubate tubes on ice for 3 minutes.

steps.title: Final Resuspension and Counting
steps.instruction: Resuspend nuclei and quantify using a hemocytometer.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 10 µL of chilled Diluted Nuclei Buffer; pipet mix 10 times and pulse vortex for one second.
Inspect and count on an epifluorescence microscope with a 7-AAD filter (peak excitation ~550 nm, peak emission ~650 nm).
For each sample, dilute 1 µL of nuclei in 11 µL of Diluted Nuclei Buffer and load 10 µL onto a hemocytometer.
